evals.name: plan-refunds-python
evals.prompt: In {repo}, my branch `wip` is a work-in-progress with a couple of things mixed into it. I want to land the refund feature onto `integration` as small reviewable PRs. Plan the PRs for me — don't create any branches yet. Save the plan to {outputs}/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: A slice plan for the refund feature only, thin path first: slice 1 issues a refund end to end (POST /orders/{id}/refunds handler, refund service, Order.apply_refund, repository save, payment client, app wiring and PAYMENT_API_URL) with the refundable-amount limit already enforced, since a refund path without it is unsafe to run; listing refunds is a later behaviour slice; every domain/repository/service method lands beside its caller; newsletter hunks excluded; count_refunds flagged as uncalled; stops before building.

evals.name: build-refunds-python
evals.prompt: In {repo}, pull the refund feature out of `wip` into stacked PRs onto `integration`. I already agree to whatever split you think is right, so don't stop to ask me — plan it and build it. There's no GitHub here: push the branches to origin, and instead of opening PRs write each PR's title, base branch and description to {outputs}/prs.md. Save your plan to {outputs}/plan.md as well.
evals.expected_output: Branches pushed to origin forming one linear stack off integration; the bottom branch already serves POST refunds end to end with PaymentClient wired and the refundable-amount limit enforced, and get_refunds/list_refunds arrive in a later slice; each branch passes `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; the tip matches wip for refund-only files and wip minus newsletter hunks for shared files; no newsletter code anywhere; prs.md lists each PR with its base.

evals.name: plan-reminders-typescript
evals.prompt: {repo} is our billing service. The `wip` branch has the invoice reminders feature plus some unrelated dark-mode UI work. Plan how to split just the reminders into stacked PRs onto `integration`. Plan only — save it to {outputs}/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: A plan in the repo's own vocabulary (entities/db/integrations/services/routes/jobs/container), thin path first: slice 1 sends one reminder end to end (whichever entrypoint — job or route — reaches it most simply, with the store, service, a channel and the container wiring it needs) and already throttled, so it never re-sends to the same invoice daily; the second channel or entrypoint is a later behaviour slice; the twilio dependency arrives with the first slice that imports the SMS client; every entity/store method beside its caller; the dark-mode files and the color dependency excluded from package.json hunks.

evals.name: first-slice-assist
evals.prompt: In {repo}, `wip` holds the assistant's tool-catalog feature: the catalog client, a catalog cache, the ask service, a customer-token debug path and the /ask endpoint. Carve it into stacked PRs onto `integration`. Plan the whole stack, but build and push only the first slice for now: the catalog client, browser-session path only — the customer-token debug path will be its own slice further up. I already agree with whatever plan you pick, so don't stop to ask. There's no GitHub here: push the branch to origin and write the PR's title, base branch and description to {outputs}/prs.md. Save the plan to {outputs}/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: One branch off integration touching only catalog_client.py and its test: no token-path imports, env reads or with_env helper; no comment citing the ToolCatalog cache; ToolSpec imported from assist_contracts 1.5 (on integration since wip forked) instead of the hand-written copy; tests rewritten to pin path, payload and encoding rather than counting calls. The plan puts tests/helpers.py with the debug slice and the LIVE_MODEL flag with the ask-service slice.

evals.name: replan-drop-refresh-kb
evals.prompt: Earlier you planned how to carve `wip` in {repo} into stacked PRs onto `integration`, and I approved it; the plan is at {fixture}/plan_v1.md. Change of scope: temporarily scope out the knowledge-refresh tooling — the crawler and the check CLI. We just need its final output, the committed index, and the runtime code that reads it. Re-plan, then build and push the first two slices of the new plan. Don't stop to ask. There's no GitHub here: push the branches to origin, write each PR's title, base branch and description to {outputs}/prs.md, and save the new plan to {outputs}/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: Two slices: slice 1 is a thin path — POST /ask answering through one capability (the gateway tool or the committed knowledge), routed and wired — and slice 2 adds the other capability. fixture_path rides only with the knowledge loader; nothing from the dropped refresh tooling (crawler, check CLI, tmp_cwd, pages.json, index_bad.jsonl, REFRESH_SOURCE_URL) survives anywhere, even though plan v1 attached the helpers to the dropped bottom slice.
files: fixture: build_fixture.py kb (writes plan_v1.md beside the repo)

evals.name: thin-path-turn
evals.prompt: In {repo}, `wip` holds the turn engine for our chat backend; the model client is already on `integration`. Carve the turn engine into stacked PRs onto `integration`. Plan the whole stack, then build and push the first two slices. I already agree with whatever plan you pick, so don't stop to ask. There's no GitHub here: push the branches to origin, write each PR's title, base branch and description to {outputs}/prs.md, and save the plan to {outputs}/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: Slice 1 is a bare working turn: TurnRequest without system_prompt, run_turn calling the model with no rules, POST /turn routed and wired with MODEL_URL. Slice 2 adds exactly one behaviour (refusal, clipping, citation retry or suggestions) with its tests; topics.json rides only with a behaviour that reads it; policy rules never land without run_turn calling them; the debug override and figures metric are planned last.

evals.name: subset-approval-turn
evals.prompt: In {repo}, I approved the plan at {fixture}/plan_v1.md for carving the turn engine out of `wip` onto `integration`. Build and push only slices 1, 3 and 4 for now — the off-topic refusal (slice 2) is still being discussed with the PM, so leave it out entirely. Don't stop to ask. There's no GitHub here: push the branches to origin, write each PR's title, base branch and description to {outputs}/prs.md, and save the plan you actually built to {outputs}/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: Three linear slices: the bare turn, clipping, suggestions. No off_topic or refusal anywhere. topics.json and topics.py (which plan v1 put in the dropped slice 2) move to the suggestions slice, which now needs them, and plan.md/prs.md says so; the plan is re-shown for the subset rather than built silently.
files: fixture: build_fixture.py turn-plan (writes plan_v1.md beside the repo)

evals.name: stale-merge-greeting
evals.prompt: In {repo}, `wip` has the follow-up suggestions for our chat backend. Carve the suggestions into stacked PRs onto `integration` and build them all. I already agree with whatever split you pick, so don't stop to ask. There's no GitHub here: push the branches to origin, write each PR's title, base branch and description to {outputs}/prs.md, and save the plan to {outputs}/plan.md.
evals.expected_output: The suggestions land (suggest.py, run_turn calling it, tests). wip merged integration and resolved its conflicts with its own older greeting code, so the three-dot diff also reverts #101's punctuation fix, comment and two tests; every slice keeps integration's version of those, and the plan names the stale merge resolution as a deviation from wip.
